subject: Concept review: Mom-facing property-map tool. Paul-chosen mechanic: tap 4–6 points on an aerial photo → SVG polygon → voice-name → zone persists → accumulates over time. Paul-reframe today: 'a visual tool to help Mom see the whole property will help her in defining areas in her own head' — browse-as-thinking-tool may need to precede or co-locate with define-mode.
review_level: screen-component (a new card/surface concept; not whole-app)

user_context.primary_user: Mom — make-or-break user [validated]. iPhone Pro 393x793, mobile-only, one-handed reclined posture, may not have reading glasses on, 2-turn engagement rhythm, photo-first ask behavior, 17:1 revisit-to-save ratio, 0 stars in 104 revisits.
core_jobs_to_be_done: JTBD #1 (validated): scan the cards and see what the place is doing today — the map could become a 6th-or-7th scan target if (and only if) it's read-at-a-glance and revisitable
JTBD #6 (inferred): take a moment that's just for the place, not any task — pure 'look at the property from above' lives squarely in this job; browse-as-thinking-tool fits cleanly
JTBD #5 (validated): low-key co-authorship (the Spiderwort / Mom-pick promotion shape) — naming a zone is the same co-authorship muscle (Mom writes her words into the dashboard's vocabulary)
Not-yet-jobs the map might catalyze: 'where is this plant?' (spatial-axis questions the dashboard cannot currently answer), 'what could I plant near the pond?' (Phase E + zoneAffinity)
user_context.context_of_use: Bed/coffee or porch/wind-down. One-handed. Half-engagement. iOS Safari. No-glasses use mode validated by 12 A/A+ events on her device.
assumptions_made: Treating 'Mom defines the zones' as a real intended interaction — but no observed behavior validates Mom wants this. She has named ONE plant (autumn bentgrass) for the canon; she has never been observed asking a spatial question of the dashboard.
Treating Paul's reframe ('browse helps her define areas in her own head') as the load-bearing insight. If the reframe is correct, this review's verdict on the mechanic shifts substantially.
Assuming the existing Step A / Step B chip pattern (Garden Guru photo flow) is the surface vocabulary Mom now knows — it's the closest analog to 'small, finite, confident decisions' she has done.
Assuming UnifiedVoice (the speech-to-text factory in viewer.html) is the reusable substrate for voice-naming. Confirmed present in current code.
user_context.user_context_confidence: medium — strong on Mom's behavior signals; weak on whether Mom-defines-zones is a behavior pattern she has shown. This concept assumes a behavior we have NOT observed (per `feedback_defer_affordances_pending_signal`).

principles_applied: Defer affordances pending signal (memory) — the load-bearing lens for this whole review
Strip teases, card holds (fernwood) — the map's placement question
Make every surface read at half-engagement (fernwood)
Glyphs follow the journal voice, not the dashboard voice (fernwood)
Caution as noticing, not warning (fernwood) — applies to the 'edit mode' framing
Meet the user at the action (cross-project)
Scope is communicated by where you tap, not auto-detected (cross-project candidate)
Patterns port, defaults don't (cross-project candidate) — Phase F's Step A / Step B chip pattern ports; the defaults shift
Don Norman — signifiers, feedback, conceptual model, perceived affordance
Project Mom reading accessibility (memory) — meaning carried by icon + size + color + position, not labels
Mom's anti-persona: 2-turn ceiling, not a multi-turn chainer
Mom's 0-stars-in-104-revisits — curation by return, not by tap
triage_summary: Paul's reframe is the most important thing in this brief. 'A visual tool to help Mom SEE the whole property' is a JTBD Mom has shown signal for (Job 6 — take a moment that's just for the place). 'Mom defines zones by tapping vertices' is a JTBD she has shown ZERO signal for (no spatial questions, no asking-about-where, 0 stars in 104 revisits — she does not curate by tapping). The right v1 ships the browse surface alone and watches what Mom does with it. If she starts revisiting the map, or starts asking spatial questions of Garden Guru, that's the signal that a define-mode is wanted. If she opens the map twice and never comes back, the define-mode would have been dead UI. The tap-to-place mechanic is a reasonable mechanic IF a define-mode is warranted — but the right mechanic per the no-glasses + 2-turn constraints is actually a hybrid: Paul pre-draws starter zones (he's already done this in `tools/draw-zones.py`), Mom voice-names what she calls them. That moves the act of creation onto Paul (who can use a desktop tool) and the act of naming onto Mom (the part that captures HER mental model of the property — which is the real value Paul's reframe is reaching for). The transition from looking → defining is solved by NOT having a transition: looking IS the surface; naming is a one-tap overlay on a pre-drawn zone, not a multi-vertex drawing flow. This concept has a strong core (the aerial map as thinking tool) wrapped in a speculative mechanic (Mom-draws-zones). Ship the core. Defer the mechanic.

findings.surface: The browse-vs-define mode split — the whole concept's structural question
findings.observation: Paul's reframe today reorders the concept's job priority. The original concept's primary value-creation step is 'Mom draws and names a zone' — define-mode is the destination, browse-mode is incidental. The reframe says: 'A visual tool to help Mom see the whole property will help her in defining areas in her own head.' Browse IS the thinking tool. Defining is downstream — and may or may not happen at her hand. Today telemetry on Mom: 0 stars in 104 revisits, 2-turn ceiling on every Garden Guru conversation, 12 A/A+ events (active accessibility constraint). She has NEVER shown a multi-step, multi-vertex authoring behavior. The closest she has come is the two-step Step A / Step B confirm chip — and that's two BINARY taps, not four to six positional vertex placements.
findings.user_impact: If Fernwood ships the full concept (browse + define together) and Mom uses it for browse but never touches define, that's a partial win — but the define-mode UI taxes the surface, adds visual chrome (vertex markers, edit toggle, undo button, voice prompt, save chip), and pulls the surface toward the task-manager voice that Caution-as-noticing rules out. If Fernwood ships browse-only first and Mom comes back to it 4 times a week, that's a stronger signal than the define-mechanic would have produced — AND Paul's reframe is validated empirically (she IS using the aerial-view to think). If she doesn't come back at all, the design avoided shipping a dead authoring surface.
findings.principle_invoked: Defer affordances pending signal (memory) — Mom has not shown the underlying interaction pattern (multi-vertex spatial authoring) the define-mode assumes. Friction kills — it just works (the simpler surface is the surface that earns daily use). Patterns port, defaults don't (the Phase F two-step chip pattern says 'binary taps work for Mom'; multi-vertex tap-to-place is a different shape entirely).
findings.recommendation: Split the concept into two phases. **Phase 1 (ship now): Browse-only.** A new 'Map' card (or 'Fernwood from above' — see F4 for naming) with the existing GEP aerial photo, Paul's pre-drawn zones (already done in `tools/draw-zones.py`), Crimson-Text zone labels at the centroids in journal voice. No edit affordances, no vertex markers, no voice prompt. Mom taps a zone → it expands with the plants/wildlife/observations associated with that zone (existing JSON), all in field-journal voice. **Phase 2 (ship only after signal): Mom-names-a-zone.** Watch Phase 1 for 30 days. Signal-to-promote is one of: (a) Mom revisits the Map card 5+ times a week (validates it's a thinking tool worth deepening), or (b) Mom asks Garden Guru a spatial question ('what could I plant near the pond,' 'what bird was that by the fairway edge'), or (c) Mom tells Paul directly that she'd like to name something. If none of those signals arrive, the define-mode is dead-on-arrival affordance and should never ship. **The alternative hybrid mechanic if Phase 2 ships:** Paul pre-draws all zones via the existing Python prototype; Mom only re-names them. Naming is a single tap on a zone label → voice modal → speech-to-text fills the new name → Step A chip ('Save as XYZ?' Yes/Not quite). This is the same pattern she already knows from Garden Guru. No vertex placement, no polygon drawing — those become Paul's job (and he's already doing them).
findings.effort: Phase 1: low-medium (one new card, render existing polygons over base image, no new mechanic). Phase 2 (only if signal): low (single voice naming flow leveraging existing UnifiedVoice + Step A chip pattern).

findings.surface: Tap-to-place vertex mechanic — IF Phase 2 (define-mode) ships
findings.observation: If define-mode does ship, the proposed mechanic (4–6 taps to place vertices, SVG polygon renders between them) has three accessibility failure modes for Mom's no-glasses context: (1) precise tap placement on an aerial photo is a fine-motor task; the typical iOS tap-target floor (44pt) is wider than 'the corner of the patio I'm trying to mark' in the photo; without zoom, every vertex tap is approximate. (2) After 3 vertices placed, the user needs to see them — vertex markers are typically small dots; at 12pt they're invisible at half-engagement; at 24pt they obscure the underlying landmarks. (3) Undoing a mis-placed vertex requires either a separate undo button (extra chrome) or tap-on-existing-vertex to remove (gesture conflict with placing the next one). The Phase F two-step chip pattern Mom knows is binary, not positional; this is a strictly harder cognitive + motor task than anything she has done in the app.
findings.user_impact: If Mom tries to draw a zone and the polygon doesn't match her mental model of the area, she has three options: redo it (4–6 more taps), accept an inaccurate zone, or abandon. All three are exits from the flow. The 2-turn ceiling she shows on Guru tells us her tolerance for multi-step authoring is low. The define-mode as proposed sits well above that tolerance.
findings.principle_invoked: Project Mom reading accessibility (memory) — meaning + intent carried by shape + size + position, not by labels or fine details. Don Norman's perceived-affordance principle — a vertex marker that is too small to see, or too big to place precisely, breaks the conceptual model. Friction kills — multi-step authoring is friction by definition.
findings.recommendation: If Phase 2 ships (which this review recommends against until signal), the tap-to-place mechanic should be replaced by the hybrid above (Paul pre-draws, Mom names) OR by a 'pinch-stretch a pre-drawn rectangle' shape that gives Mom 4 corner handles to drag instead of 4 taps to place. The handle mechanic gives her continuous feedback (the rectangle deforms in real time), uses 44pt+ handles, and degrades gracefully (if she gives up halfway, the rectangle is still a valid shape, not an open polygon). But — to be clear — if Mom-defines-zones is the goal, the cleanest mechanic per her observed behavior is voice-naming a pre-drawn shape. Drawing is the wrong interaction shape for her telemetry. Required tap target: 48pt minimum for any vertex marker or handle. Required undo affordance: a single 'Undo' text button (16pt, sentence-case) above the photo, NOT a tiny rewind glyph.
findings.effort: Phase 2 mechanic redesign: medium. The recommendation is to skip this entirely and use voice-naming-on-pre-drawn-shape, which is low effort.

findings.surface: The browse-as-thinking-tool surface — what Mom sees when she opens 'Map'
findings.observation: Paul's reframe asks: 'help her see the whole property.' The question is what she sees first. Three options: (a) aerial photo, no overlays, no labels — pure imagery, unmediated. (b) aerial photo + pre-drawn zone outlines, no labels — the structure of the property is suggested but unnamed. (c) aerial photo + zones + Paul's labels (Western patio, Pond area, Front lawn, Fairway meadow, Western fairway edge) — fully mediated, immediately legible. The reframe argues that 'looking is the thinking tool' — which suggests (a) or (b). But the no-glasses + half-engagement constraints argue strongly for (c) — Mom needs the surface to read at glance, and an unmediated aerial photo at 393pt wide is hard to parse (the house is ~50pt across; landmarks she might recognize visually are mostly trees-and-roof-and-driveway at that scale). The right answer is (c) with a tonal restraint — Paul's labels are present but quiet, Crimson Text italic at 14pt, positioned at zone centroids, on translucent backgrounds (not the white-pill chips from the Python prototype, which look like dashboard tag-pills not journal labels). Mom recognizes the house, the pond, the driveway because the labels tell her — but they don't shout, and the photo itself is still the dominant element.
findings.user_impact: If Mom opens 'Map' and sees an aerial photo at 393pt with no labels, the first 1.5 seconds register as 'a fuzzy green blob' — and she taps back out, never returning. Half-engagement bar fails. If she sees labels in dashboard-voice (white pills, uppercase tracking), the surface reads as ops-map / Google Maps chrome — not field journal. The right register is journal-labels-on-photograph: Crimson Text italic, faint cream background pill at 70% opacity, centered on the zone, sized for no-glasses legibility (≥16pt). The photo carries the visceral 'this is my place from above'; the labels carry the cognitive 'these are the parts I know.' Paul's instinct that 'looking IS the thinking' is right — the labels don't fight the photograph; they index into it.
findings.principle_invoked: Make every surface read at half-engagement (fernwood). Tone-coherence across all chrome (fernwood) — labels-as-pills is the wrong register here. Typographic hierarchy by value (cross-project) — the photo is the lead; the labels are the index. Glyphs follow the journal voice (fernwood) — generalizes to zone-labels.
findings.recommendation: Default state when Mom opens 'Map': aerial photo + 5–7 pre-drawn zones from Paul's existing prototype (drop forest-interior — it'd cover everything; keep it in a legend-line below the photo if at all). Zone labels: Crimson Text italic, 16pt, dark forest green text (#2a4f33) on cream pill (#faf7ed at 80% opacity), centered at zone centroid. NO uppercase tracking. NO chips. NO color-coded zone fills like the Python prototype's bright purple/orange/blue (those are debugging colors — they shout in dashboard voice). Replace zone-fill with quiet sage outlines (#9ab48a, 1.5px stroke) over the photo with very low fill alpha (~12% of an in-palette green) — the zone is suggested, not screamed. The photograph stays the visceral lead. Below the photo, a single italic Crimson line: 'Fernwood from above — leaf-off, March 2015.' Mom opens the card, sees her place, knows where she is. That's the thinking tool. Tap any label → see plants/wildlife/observations in that zone, rendered like an Almanac entry.
findings.effort: low-medium (SVG overlay rendering Paul's existing polygons over the existing PNG; CSS for journal-voice label pills; tap-zone-to-expand wiring)

findings.observation: The concept refers to 'the map view' / 'the property map.' Both are dashboard-voice (Google Maps, Apple Maps, ops-map). A field-journal name carries the surface's intent better: 'Fernwood from above,' 'The property,' 'Looking down,' 'Aerial view' (last is borderline). Per the F5 audit today (dashboard stack policy is deferred), this card's placement is open — but D2 needs a call BEFORE this ships. The Property card already exists at #card-property (the 6th strip tile, currently rendering 'Fernwood' as the label). Two real options: (A) Map replaces or absorbs the Property card — they're about the same thing (this is your place), one is data-and-numbers, the other is imagery. (B) Map is a new card with its own strip tile, requiring D2 to land as 'tiered strip with everything gets a tile.'
findings.user_impact: Option (A): the Property card today gets 45 views on Mom's device — not the top, but not at the bottom. If the Map absorbs the Property card and becomes the new face of 'this is your place from above,' it inherits real engagement and gives Mom an aerial-photo entry point into all the property-state info (elevation, frost dates, soils, microclimate) she currently has to scroll through. Option (B): a fresh card with no strip tile becomes Worth Considering all over again — 5 views vs 60 for the cards in the strip. The map-as-thinking-tool only works if she opens it; she only opens it if the strip carries it.
findings.principle_invoked: Strip teases, card holds (fernwood) — the map without a strip seat is off the menu. Tone-coherence across all chrome — 'map view' is dashboard-voice; 'Fernwood from above' is journal-voice. Make every surface read at half-engagement — the strip-tile lead text is what makes her tap.
findings.recommendation: **Strong recommendation: Option (A) — absorb the Property card.** Replace the existing 'Fernwood' tile in the strip with one that leads with imagery + a single evocative line. Strip tile: a small (~120pt × 80pt) version of the aerial photo as the tile background, Crimson Text title 'Fernwood' at the bottom-left in cream over a dark-green gradient (so it remains legible without competing). Sub-line stays journal-voice: 'On Cherokee land · Blue Ridge thermal belt' OR (more evocatively) 'The property from above — and what it holds.' Card title (when she taps in): 'Fernwood' (single word, Crimson Text 24pt) — same as the strip. The card body opens with the aerial photo at full width, then the existing property-spec content (elevation, frost, soils, microclimate) moves below the photo. **The map is not a new card; it's the new face of the Property card.** This sidesteps D2 entirely (no new strip tile needed), gives the map immediate Mom-eyes engagement via an existing 45-view card, and unifies what was previously two separate ideas (the Property card's spec-sheet voice + the new spatial surface). Property as the spec-sheet card has been a tone-leak risk all along (today's portfolio audit F2-from-the-2026-05-11-review flagged it as spec-sheet voice); replacing the front with a photograph absorbs that problem too.
findings.effort: medium — refactor Property card to lead with aerial photo + zone overlay; preserve existing data below; update strip tile to imagery-backed lead.

findings.surface: Voice-naming flow — IF Phase 2 (define / re-name) ships
findings.observation: The proposed flow has Mom voice-name the zone AFTER she draws it. Two issues: (a) the voice prompt at end-of-drawing is poorly-timed — she has been concentrating on placing vertices, the speech-recognition modal pops up, she has to context-switch from a fine-motor task to a verbal one. (b) iOS Safari's SpeechRecognition support is uneven — it works in Safari 14.5+ but can fail silently on first-use (permission prompt missed) and on flaky cellular (network-bound speech). The existing UnifiedVoice in viewer.html (`createVoiceCapture`, line ~10408) is already wired and handles these gracefully (`isSupported()` check, error states with `.ui-mic-hint.error`). That's the substrate to lean on.
findings.user_impact: If voice-naming pops up after a 4–6-vertex drawing flow and recognition fails, Mom is now staring at an unnamed polygon with no recovery path she understands. If it works, she has named her zone — but she has spent 30–60 seconds on this single zone, which is 5–15x longer than any flow she currently does in the app. The 2-turn rhythm tells us this stretches her tolerance.
findings.principle_invoked: Friction kills — it just works. Meet the user at the action — naming a zone IS the action; placing vertices is incidental motor work. Save-success at the surface, not at the destination (candidate) — the named zone should render its new name at the input location, not require scrolling.
findings.recommendation: If Phase 2 ships per the hybrid (Paul pre-draws, Mom names): the flow is — Mom long-taps a zone label → modal appears with the existing label visible + a 🎤 button (52pt+, journal-voice copy 'Hold to rename this place') → she taps-and-holds, speaks, releases → speech-to-text fills a textbox + a Step A chip appears: 'Save as [transcribed text]?' (Yes / Not quite). Yes commits the rename; Not quite re-opens the modal with the text in a textbox she can type-edit. The Step A chip is the pattern she already knows from Garden Guru. **Fallback if SpeechRecognition is unsupported or fails:** the modal opens with the existing label as editable text in a 18pt textbox + same Step A chip below — typing is the path, voice is the upgrade. **Label position after rename:** in the same location on the map (don't move it). Font: Crimson Text italic 16pt (matches F3). Size at no-glasses floor: ≥16pt. **What NOT to do:** auto-detect when she stops speaking and auto-save (silently). Auto-save here is the 2026-05-22 silent-misroute failure all over again. Explicit Yes-tap before commit.
findings.effort: low-medium (reuse UnifiedVoice; reuse Step A chip CSS; new modal + rename wiring). Note: only build IF Phase 1 signal warrants Phase 2.

findings.surface: The 'transition from looking → defining' — Paul's question 3
findings.observation: Paul asks: how does Mom go from 'I'm looking at the property' to 'I want to name this place' without an edit-mode toggle that fights her one-handed leisure-reading posture? The clean answer per this review's overall verdict: **she doesn't transition, because v1 doesn't have a define-mode at all.** But if Phase 2 ships, the question is real. Two anti-patterns to avoid: (a) a persistent 'Edit' button at the top of the map card — adds chrome to every browse session, register-leak toward task-manager / CMS-admin voice. (b) auto-detecting intent from interaction (long-tap = rename, short-tap = browse, etc.) — auto-detection is the exact pattern Mom's 2026-05-22 silent-misroute taught us to avoid. The Phase F two-step chip pattern is the right shape: an explicit, in-context, journal-voice affordance that the user taps deliberately. The trigger Paul names as a candidate — 'photo-attached (a Garden Guru reply chip)' — is the strongest one. If Mom IDs a Spiderwort via Garden Guru, the reply could include a Step C chip: 'Where on the property?' (tap a zone). That's the same pattern she already knows (Step A 'Does that look right?', Step B 'Worth adding to the Almanac?', new Step C 'Where on the property?'). It lives on her existing killer flow; it doesn't add chrome to the map card.
findings.user_impact: The transition pattern Paul names (photo-attached chip from Garden Guru) is exactly the kind of trigger Mom has already validated. The alternative (button on the map view) violates the journal-not-task-manager principle by definition — 'Edit' is a task-manager verb. The chip-after-photo pattern carries the affordance to her existing flow rather than asking her to come to a new flow.
findings.principle_invoked: Scope is communicated by where you tap, not auto-detected (candidate). Patterns port, defaults don't (candidate) — the Step A/B chip pattern ports as Step C. Friction kills — it just works. Caution as noticing, not warning — 'Edit mode' is the wrong register entirely.
findings.recommendation: **Strong recommendation: if Phase 2 ships, the rename trigger is the Garden Guru photo-reply chip, NOT a button on the map card.** After a successful species_promoted, append a third chip: 'Where on the property? (tap a zone)' → Mom taps → modal slides up showing the aerial photo with the zone labels → she taps a zone → that observation is now associated with that zone in JSON. If she wants to rename WHILE in the modal, a small italic Crimson 'rename this place' link under each zone label opens the voice-naming flow from F5. This puts the spatial-naming affordance ON the path Mom already uses, doesn't add chrome to the standalone map card, and uses the muscle memory she's built. **The map card itself stays browse-only — no Edit button, no edit-mode toggle, no vertex markers visible at rest.** Rename / re-zone is something that happens FROM the Garden Guru flow, not as a separate mode in the map.
findings.effort: low (add Step C chip to Phase F flow; add modal-from-chip; reuse F3's map render).

findings.surface: 'She drew this' — Mom's ownership of named zones (Paul's question 6)
findings.observation: Paul asks: what's the affordance that says 'this is yours, you can change it' without producing edit-mode noise? This is the same question the star tried to answer for entries — and the star is dying because the answer was 'no overt affordance is needed.' For zones, the parallel: if Mom can rename a zone (F5 / F6), the renaming itself is the ownership signal — the label now reads in her voice. No 'Mom's pick' purple chip needed (the chip-pattern is failing on the Worth Considering card per today's F6 finding). No 'Edit' / 'Delete' buttons sitting on every zone label. The implicit trust model: any zone is renamable via long-tap (or via the Step C chip from Garden Guru); the renaming flow itself shows her the existing name and lets her change it. Discoverability: a one-line italic Crimson hint below the photo, surfaced ONCE on first visit and dismissable — 'Long-tap a label to rename it.' After that, no chrome.
findings.user_impact: If the affordance is 'long-tap = rename,' there's nothing on the card to telegraph that to Mom. She might never discover it. BUT — given that the recommended primary entry is via the Garden Guru chip flow (F6), discoverability of long-tap is less critical: she'll learn the renaming pattern via the chip first, and long-tap becomes a power-user shortcut. The single first-visit hint is the bridge.
findings.principle_invoked: Ornament earns its place — chips and Edit buttons that don't see use are tax. Defer affordances pending signal — Delete is an affordance she may never want; don't ship it until she asks. Friction kills.
findings.recommendation: **Delete affordance: do NOT ship in Phase 2.** Zero observed signal that Mom deletes anything in the app today. If she renames a zone wrong, she renames it again — that's the recovery path. Add Delete only if Mom asks for it directly. **Rename discoverability: a single Crimson italic hint, first visit only, dismissed on first dismiss-tap.** Stored in localStorage as `tateTracker.mapHintSeen`. **The 'she drew this' trust signal IS the renamed label itself** — when she sees 'The pond' rendered in journal voice at the zone centroid, that's the recognition. No chip, no badge, no purple. **One additional softer signal:** if she has renamed a zone, the entry-render of any observation associated with that zone could include a line: 'In ' + (her zone name) — e.g., 'In The pond' — reinforcing her authorship without adding chrome.
findings.effort: low (first-visit hint + state flag; no delete affordance).

findings.surface: Zone schema and the relationship to existing JSON (plants.json, mammals.json, observations)
findings.observation: The existing `tools/draw-zones.py` uses fractional (0–1) coordinates with hardcoded zones. That's a Paul-only authoring artifact, not a Mom-facing schema. For Phase 1 (browse-only) to work, zones need to live in a JSON file with stable IDs (`zoneId`), names (`label`), polygons (fractional coords, copied straight from the Python prototype), and optionally a Mom-facing display name when she has renamed (`displayLabel`). Plants and wildlife reference zoneIds in their existing records (`zoneAffinity: ['pond-area', 'spring-drainage']`). The CLAUDE.md pickup line under 'Plants to consider planting' notes this: 'once zones lock, populate per candidate so Phase E can answer what could I plant near the pond?' This concept is the trigger for that schema to land.
findings.user_impact: Without zone IDs in the data, the map card has nothing to expand into when Mom taps a zone. The whole 'tap-to-see-what's-in-this-zone' value falls apart. The schema is load-bearing for browse-mode making the card worth opening twice.
findings.principle_invoked: Meet the user at the action — tapping a zone is the action; the action's payoff is seeing what's IN the zone. Without the schema connecting zones to existing data, the action has no payoff. Single source of truth per concept (memory) — zone definitions should live in one place (`zones.json`), not get duplicated between Python and viewer.html.
findings.recommendation: Ship a new `zones.json` at repo root with the shape `{zones: [{id, label, displayLabel?, polygon: [[x_frac, y_frac], ...], baseLayer: 'gep-2015-03-leafoff.png'}, ...]}` populated from `tools/draw-zones.py`. Inline it into viewer.html as `ZONES_DATA` per the existing pattern. Add a `zoneAffinity: [zoneId, ...]` array to relevant plants in `plants.json` (start small — maybe 5–6 of the 17 plants Paul knows the location of; leave the rest blank). When Mom taps a zone, the expanded view filters plants/wildlife/observations by zoneAffinity. **If Paul wants to rename a zone via the Python prototype (his own workflow), he edits zones.json directly; the viewer reflects on next deploy.** Mom's renames (if/when Phase 2 ships) write `displayLabel` to a different JSON or to localStorage — keep authorship lanes separate.
findings.effort: medium (zones.json structure + ZONES_DATA inline + zone-tap expand wiring + 5–6 plant zoneAffinity backfills).

findings.observation: Paul asks: what observed behavior would tell us this is working? What would tell us it's not? Per the broader 'Defer affordances pending signal' pattern, the gates need to be named in writing BEFORE Phase 1 ships, so the decision to promote (or kill) Phase 2 is empirical, not vibes.
findings.user_impact: n/a — this is forward-direction, not a current-issue finding
findings.principle_invoked: Defer affordances pending signal (memory) — explicit promotion gates are the operational form of the principle.
findings.recommendation: **Working signals (Phase 1 'browse-only' is earning its place):** (a) Mom's device shows ≥3 'Map' card_section_viewed events per week for 2 consecutive weeks. (b) Mom expands the card and taps at least one zone (zone_tapped event — needs to be instrumented) more than once. (c) During the T+30 Mom interview, Mom mentions the map unprompted ('I like seeing the pond from above'). Any one of (a)/(b)/(c) = working. **Promote-Phase-2 signals (define/rename mode is warranted):** (a) Mom asks Garden Guru a spatial question — 'what's near the pond,' 'what's the name of that area by the driveway' (needs Guru conversation review). (b) Mom tells Paul directly she'd like to call something a different name. (c) Mom revisits the Map card 5+ times a week (heavy revisit = thinking tool is real, deepening with naming is justified). Two-of-three = promote. **Not-working signals (kill the surface):** (a) Mom opens the Map card ≤1x in two weeks. (b) When she opens it, she expands the card 0 times (just glances and closes). (c) T+30 interview: Mom can't recall the Map card exists or describes it as 'the one I don't really use.' Two-of-three = retire (rare for Fernwood — but the discipline matters). **Add a question to the T+30 Mom interview slate:** 'Have you opened the Map / Fernwood from above? principles_to_propose.principle: Browse before author — show before ask to make
principles_to_propose.scope: cross-project candidate (Fernwood is first instance; would apply to houseplants if it grows a similar 'map your collection' shape, and to anything with user-generated structure)
principles_to_propose.rationale: The pattern this review surfaces: when a concept's value depends on the user doing structured authoring (drawing, tagging, classifying, organizing), the first ship should be the read-only view of pre-authored content. The reader's behavior on the read-only surface tells you whether the author-mode is wanted, and what shape it should take. Mom's telemetry has 0 stars in 104 revisits — the same pattern we'd see if a draw-mode shipped without first proving the see-mode is wanted. The principle generalizes 'Defer affordances pending signal' specifically for concepts where the assumed user behavior is creation/structuring. Second occurrence for validation: when a future Paul concept proposes user-driven structure (zone-naming, plant-tagging, collection-building, anything), the principle says ship the read-only view first. If/when this principle applies a second time, it's promotable to canon.

principles_to_propose.principle: The strip-tile is imagery when it can be — words when it has to be
principles_to_propose.rationale: Today's strip tiles are all text-led (Crimson Text titles + DM Sans sub-copy). For most cards (Weather, Plants, Wildlife, Celestial) that's correct — the lead is a piece of evocative writing pulled from that card. But for the Property card and the proposed Map card, the visceral lead IS an image (a photograph of the place from above). When a card's primary value is imagery, the strip tile should preview the imagery — a small (~120pt × 80pt) thumbnail with the title overlaid, not a text-only summary. This sharpens the 'Strip teases' rule with a media-type carveout. Second occurrence: when a future card has imagery as its lead value (a wildlife-cam card, a seasonal-photo card, anything photo-led), the same imagery-as-tile rule applies.

Two convergent patterns in this review: (a) define-mode is dead UI for Mom's 2-turn, no-glasses, photo-first profile, and (b) the right place to surface a 'name this' or 'tag this' or 'where is this' affordance is INSIDE her existing killer flow (Garden Guru photo reply), not as a separate authoring mode on a separate surface. This is the 'patterns port, defaults don't' candidate principle's specific application to Fernwood: the Step A / Step B chip pattern is the authoring vocabulary Mom knows. Any new authoring affordance should be a Step C/D/E chip on the same flow, not a new surface. Second occurrence: when Phase G observations-as-knowledge surfaces, the same principle says — observation-tagging happens via a chip on the Almanac entry, not via an Edit button on each entry.
